objective: Turn comprehensive weekly evidence into a small commitment slate while preserving gathering purpose, voluntary agency, paid-work boundaries, privacy, and human authority.

highest_impact_finding.finding: A weekly protocol intended to reduce burden proposed a 60-minute operator budget; all behavioral invariants passed while the reader-burden criterion failed.
highest_impact_finding.fix: Reduce the operator budget to 30 minutes without changing the one-page decision surface or any hard gate.

error_analysis.finding: The 17 cases encode observed project-specific failure modes: commitment proliferation, preservation-obligation collapse, purposeless gathering, inferred ownership, unpaid bespoke work, privacy leakage, automation overreach, and surveillance.
error_analysis.limitation: Synthetic cases do not establish real-world usability; a separate human-reviewed two-week private canary remains required after acceptance.

evaluator_design.finding: Objective policy boundaries use deterministic binary decisions and exact reason codes rather than an LLM judge or similarity metric.

judge_validation.finding: No LLM judge is used for this RFC gate. Future qualitative canary interpretation must not be presented as a calibrated judge without human labels.

human_review.finding: The evaluator can establish structural consistency but cannot accept the RFC, choose priorities, assign people, validate lived usefulness, or authorize publication.

labeled_data.finding: There are no completed real weekly cycles labeled for reduced mental load, improved closure, or distributed agency.

bounded_change.description: Reduce only the proposed weekly operator budget from 60 minutes to 30 minutes while retaining the one-page decision surface, three-commitment default, one-in-one-out admission, one governing verb, closure receipt, voluntary ownership, commercial boundary, three-plane information placement, and human gates.

human_gates_remaining: paid-work written authorization or bounded donation
